core_obligations: Show the presheaf is Zar-sheaf (proof lines 7689-7693): with G the presheaf (f : Y -> X) maps to Gamma(Y, f^{-1}F), it is immediate from the definitions and the sheaf axioms on Y that G is a sheaf for the Zar topology.

Reduce to injectivity and gluing for qc coverings (proof lines 7696-7711): by the criterion for the qc topology it suffices that G(Y) -> H^0(V, G) is an isomorphism for every qc covering V; injectivity follows because a qc covering is surjective and equality of sections can be detected at stalks, so G is separated and it remains to show that every degree-zero Cech element becomes a global section after refining the covering.

Produce the candidate global section (proof lines 7713-7732): identifying G with the pullback of f^{-1}F along g_i : Y_i -> Y, refine the covering so that each Y_i -> Y factors through an open W_i of Y with a section t_i restricting to s_i; the compatibility of the s_i on Y_i x_Y Y_j shows that the stalk values t_{i,y} agree wherever two indices are defined, so a well-defined element (t_y) of the stalks is obtained.

Show the element is a global section (proof lines 7734-7745): working locally on Y and using the qc character of the covering to cover a neighbourhood of an arbitrary point by finitely many quasi-compact pieces, one shrinks the neighbourhood so that finitely many of the t_{i_j} agree on it, and then (t_y) is seen to come from that section.

Identify the resulting sheaf with the pullbacks (proof lines 7747-7760): in both topologies the pullback of pi_X^{-1}F is the sheafification of the presheaf (f : Y -> X) maps to the colimit of F(U) over opens U containing f(Y); sheafifying in the Zar topology produces exactly G, and since G is a qc sheaf it also computes the pullback in the qc topology.
proof_roadmap: Note that the presheaf in question is a Zariski sheaf for trivial reasons.
Reduce the qc sheaf condition to injectivity, which follows from surjectivity of qc coverings and detection of equality at stalks, and to gluing after refinement via the plus construction.

Refine the covering so that each piece factors through an open of the base, glue the local sections into a well-defined family of stalk values, and then turn it into a global section using the quasi-compactness present in the qc covering.
Finally compare with the explicit description of the pullback as a sheafification of a colimit presheaf, which identifies the sheaf with pi_X^{-1}F and with epsilon_X^{-1}pi_X^{-1}F.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the sheaf (f : Y -> X) maps to Gamma(Y, f^{-1}F) on the qc site of locally quasi-compact spaces as the pullback of F along the projections to the Zariski and qc topologies (statement lines 7674-7686). The proof has three genuinely different parts. The Zar-sheaf property is immediate (proof lines 7689-7693), but the qc-sheaf property is not: by the sheaf criterion one must prove injectivity, which uses surjectivity of qc coverings and detection of equality at stalks, and then gluing after refinement via the plus construction (proof lines 7696-7711). The gluing itself requires two steps, first manufacturing a compatible family of stalk values from local sections over opens W_i of the base (proof lines 7713-7732) and then showing that family is a global section by covering a neighbourhood of an arbitrary point with finitely many quasi-compact pieces and shrinking until finitely many local sections agree (proof lines 7734-7745). Finally the identification with the pullbacks follows by comparing with the explicit colimit description of the pullback and its sheafification (proof lines 7747-7760). The claim is H2: three separate arguments, of which the second is a real topological gluing argument.
